title: PWHL teams announce protected players during four-team expansion process
content:
The PWHL’s eight existing teams have decided which players they’ll protect from their expansion roster-building process.

During Phase 1 of the six-phase process, which began Tuesday, teams were permitted to protect three players from being signed — or selected, if necessary — by the league’s newest teams in Detroit, Hamilton, Las Vegas and San Jose.

Only players under contract for the 2026-27 season could be protected, which meant free agents needed to sign before 3 p.m. ET on Wednesday. Any signing automatically counted as one of the team’s three protections.

The four expansion teams will begin to build their inaugural rosters from the remaining pool of eligible players, which includes U.S. Olympic gold medalists Hilary Knight and Hannah Bilka, Swiss star forward Alina Müller and Canadian Daryl Watts.

Each expansion team will have a three-day window, starting Friday, to acquire five players through signings and, if necessary, a player selection process. Existing teams can lose a maximum of three players who are under contract for the 2026-27 season during this phase.
